coverage.target: performance-design.md §1/§4: one mutation on submit, Submit disabled while in flight, success line and grant rendered from the 201 body, no automatic follow-up read; MSW suite asserts one request per submit

performance-design.md §2: the shipped `RequestOptions.deadlineMs` + AbortController + DeadlineError (client.ts:165-199) is reused; `requestSupportGrant`, `listMyGrants` and `fetchSupportMetadata` pass 15_000; typed values kept on timeout; no spinner past the deadline

performance-design.md §3/§8: `useMyGrants` gated on `role === "support"`, `staleTime: 0`, explicit `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`/`refetchInterval: false`, refetched only by Check status; the 20-row bound is U3's constant; the p95 is an acknowledged measurement gap with U3 named as owner

performance-design.md §5: `useSupportMetadata` enabled on the clock-derived active status with `staleTime: 10_000`, one read per grant plus Refresh; the complete projection or a retryable error; U3's 500 ms fan-out is not this unit's budget

performance-design.md §6: the shipped `useGrantClock` 30-second tick and expiry timeout, shared `now` from the shell; remaining minutes as text, 'less than a minute left' for zero, local *Expired* with no request
performance-design.md §1: sign-in is out of scope — the shell reuses `src/auth/session.ts`; U9 adds no auth call and no refresh loop
performance-design.md §3/§4: the console's `retry: false` for queries and mutations is inherited by every U9 hook; no hook sets retry or retryDelay; a failing MSW handler is called exactly once
performance-design.md §7: the shipped `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` (client.ts:41) renders its own state with the seconds from `Retry-After`; manual control only, no automatic second request

performance-design.md §3: both U9 queries set `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `refetchInterval: false` explicitly because the console client leaves TanStack Query's default `true`; the suite asserts focus and timer issue no request

performance-design.md §5 + security-design.md §2: a route-level 403 calls `onAccessEnded`, which clears the `["support", …]` keys and drops the metadata key; the panel unmounts; a remount renders no cached projection
performance-design.md §5: the filter narrows already-returned rows in component state, issues no request and cannot widen the projection; the 20-row bound is the server's

security-design.md §1: every U9 data call is a /v1 gateway path over TLS; the console's existing Supabase Auth and Google Fonts origins are recorded, and U9 adds no origin (no CDN data, analytics, telemetry or font)

security-design.md §4 (D-U9-1): the reason is body-only, `X-Support-Reason` is retired, and `support-console/README.md:29,33` plus the gateway upstream comment are corrected in the same change; no case data in a URL

security-design.md §2: memory-only session reused; no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookie writes for token, grant id, reason draft, filter text or projection; nothing survives a reload beyond a fresh `mine` read
security-design.md §2: no JWT decode or validation for a decision; the session role decides only what is offered; every route re-authorises server-side from the forwarded token

security-design.md §3: S1, S2 and S3 are all declared in the gateway's deny-by-default table and re-checked in Identity; S2 is a support-role route owned by U3; no browser path reaches a service directly

security-design.md §2/§3: `useMyGrants` is enabled only for `role === "support"`; a route-level 403 from S2/S3 calls the scoped `clearSupportQueries`, leaving an admin's `["admin", …]` cache intact, while 401/sign-out/expiry keep the full `client.clear()`

security-design.md §2: grant, reason draft, filter and projection are memory-only; the full cache clear on 401/sign-out/expiry is unchanged; the reload path recovers the grant only through the `mine` re-read

security-design.md §3: S1 20/min and S3 60/min per token as declared by the gateway; S2 has no per-route budget and is stated as the shared per-caller-address budget rather than an invented per-token limit; a per-route limit for S2 is U3's optional addition to the route
security-design.md §3/§6: the in-process per-replica limiter scope is stated as the honest bound; a 429 is its own non-retried state with `Retry-After`

security-design.md §5: the projection is exactly userId, displayName, emailVerified, accounts[] and portfolios[]; excluded classes (subject, hash, tokens, wallet address, credentials, holdings, balances, valuations, transactions, orders) have no route and no field
security-design.md §5: `pickSupportMetadata` keeps the whitelist, drops over-sent fields and throws on a malformed projection rather than rendering a partial one; no component receives a raw response
security-design.md §4/§5: the reason travels in the create body only, is never pre-filled or echoed, and never reaches a URL, header, log, telemetry event or storage; the header path is retired

security-design.md §3/§5: errors show status and correlation id only, `ProblemDetails.detail` is never rendered; S1's two 403 causes share the neutral 'This request is not allowed.' line with the typed values kept
security-design.md §5: React's default escaping; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in this unit; server strings render as text

security-design.md §5 names the obligation: this unit writes and reads no audit record; it renders the read-audit statement and no audit content, id or retained personal data — the write is U3's, in C9
logical-components.md §5: no schema, role or data-access code in this unit; S2 reads through Identity's own grant store under Identity's role and is U3's method and route
security-design.md §7: four statuses only (pending_approval, active, expired, revoked); C5's `denied` has no producer and is not modelled; the status rendered is always the server's answer

security-design.md §7 + performance-design.md §6: the local status is a clock-derived view of the last answer; null or unparseable `expiresAt` on an active grant is treated as expired (fail closed); the server's 403 marks access ended
security-design.md §3/§7: every client-side gate is presentational; a tampered client receives 403 from the server and the screen renders the not-allowed or access-ended state with the correlation id
security-design.md §7: role and status come from the signed token and the server's answers at request time; the 60-minute window is computed by the server at approval and only displayed here
security-design.md §8: labelled regions with visible headings, accounts table caption and scope=col headers, labelled filter, keyboard operation throughout, no motion-dependent interaction

security-design.md §8: visible labels with `aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` per field; request result, status change and read completion announced in `role="status" aria-live="polite"`; access-ended and failures are `role="alert"`
security-design.md §8: `StatusBadge` renders label + tone + shape for the four statuses from `grantStatusPresentation`; urgency carried in text; Parchment Ledger tokens only
security-design.md §8: filter and every control keyboard-operable; reading order keeps the metadata-only reminder before the projection
security-design.md §8 + logical-components.md §1: every rendered state in every U9 suite passes jest-axe; a state without an axe assertion is a review-time defect
security-design.md §9: `expiresAt` and `lastSyncedAt` through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; whole-number minutes with 'less than a minute left' for zero; no raw timestamp or epoch value

security-design.md §9: the design records the English/Vietnamese half as deferred, not met — the console has no i18n module; U9 adds copy the console's way and forks no second mechanism; the deferral is tracked as decision ab46b27b with a console-wide localisation unit as owner
security-design.md §9: `Intl` degrades to its default rather than an empty or malformed date; every status renders as a word from the presentation mapping
